text: A projectile is launched at an angle '$α$' with the horizontal with a velocity $20 ms^{-1}$. After 10 s, its inclination with horizontal is '$β$'. The value of tan$β$ will be : $(g = 10 ms^{-2})$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At $t=0$, the motion of projectile is given as


[IMG]


$\tan α=\frac{u_{y}}{u_{x}}$

where, $u_{y}$ is the vertical component of initial velocity and $u_{x}$ is the horizontal component of initial velocity.

At $t=10\mathrm{s}$, the motion of projectile is given as


[IMG]


$\tan β=\frac{v_{y}}{v_{x}}$ .........(ii)

where, $v_{y}$ is the vertical component of final velocity after $t=10\mathrm{s}$ and $v_{x}$ is the horizontal component of final velocity. 

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\frac{\tan β}{\tan α}=\frac{v_{y}}{u_{y}}(~$ as $v_{x}=u_{x}$ ) ....(iii)

Using the following equation in vertical direction, we get

$\begin{array}{l} v_{y}=u_{y}-gt \\  \\ v_{y}=u_{y}-100 \end{array}$

Using Eq. (iii)

$\frac{\tan β}{\tan α}=\frac{u_{y}-100}{u_{y}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\tan β}{\tan α}=1-\dfrac{100}{u_{y}}=1-\dfrac{100}{20\sin α}(\because u_{y}=20\sin α) \end{array}$

$=1-\frac{5}{\sin α}$

$\Rightarrow \tan β=\tan α\left (1-\frac{5}{\sin α}\right )=\tan α-5\sec α$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text: A girl standing on road holds her umbrella at 45${}^{\circ }$ with the vertical to keep the rain away. If she starts running without umbrella with a speed of 15$\sqrt{2}$ kmh$^{-1}$, the rain drops hit her head vertically. The speed of rain drops with respect to the moving girl is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the girl at rest the umbrella is held at $45^{\circ }$ to the vertical, so the velocity of rain relative to the ground makes $45^{\circ }$ with the vertical and its horizontal and vertical components are equal: $v_{x}=v_{y}\tan 45^{\circ }=v_{y}$.

When she runs with $15\sqrt{2}\text{km h}^{-1}$ along the horizontal component of the rain's velocity, the rain hits her vertically, so the horizontal component of the relative velocity is zero:

$v_{x}-15\sqrt{2}=0\Rightarrow v_{x}=15\sqrt{2}\text{km h}^{-1}\Rightarrow v_{y}=15\sqrt{2}\text{km h}^{-1}$

The velocity of rain relative to the running girl is then purely vertical and equal to $v_{y}$:

$v_{\text{rain, girl}}=15\sqrt{2}=\dfrac{30}{\sqrt{2}}\text{km h}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The law of gravitation holds good for any pair of bodies in the universe.

Statement II : The weight of any person becomes zero when the person is at the centre of the earth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is true. Newton's law of universal gravitation states that every particle of matter in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the particles and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers. This law applies to any pair of bodies in the universe.

Statement II is also true. The weight of an object is the force of gravity acting on it. If a person were at the center of the Earth, the gravitational pull from all the surrounding mass of the Earth would cancel out, resulting in zero net gravitational force and therefore zero weight.

Therefore, Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true, is the correct answer.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text:
What percentage of kinetic energy of a moving particle is transferred to a stationary particle when it strikes the stationary particle of 5 times its mass?

(Assume the collision to be head-on elastic collision)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a head on elastic collision

$v_{2}=\frac{mu_{1}}{m+5m}+\frac{mu_{1}}{m+5m}$

$=\frac{2u_{1}}{6}$ or $\frac{u_{1}}{3}$

Initial kinetic energy of first mass $=\frac{1}{2}mu_{1}^{2}$

Final kinetic energy of second mass

$=\frac{1}{2}\times 5m\left (\frac{u_{1}}{3}\right )^{2}$

$=\frac{5}{9}\left (\frac{1}{2}mu_{1}^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ kinetic energy transferred = 55% of initial kinetic energy of first colliding mass
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift

text: The velocity of a small ball of mass 'm' and density $d_{1}$, when dropped in a container filled with glycerin, becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerin is $d_{2}$, then the viscous force acting on the ball, will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Viscous force acting on the ball will be equal and opposite to net of weight and buoyant force

$\Rightarrow F_{0}=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}d_{1}g-\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}d_{2}g$

$=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}d_{1}g\left (1-\frac{d_{2}}{d_{1}}\right )$

$=mg\left (1-\frac{d_{2}}{d_{1}}\right )$

text: A pendulum of length 2 m consists of a wooden bob of mass 50 g. A bullet of mass 75 g is fired towards the stationary bob with a speed v. The bullet emerges out of the bob with a speed $\frac{v}{3}$ and the bob just completes the vertical circle. The value of v is $___________ ms^{-1}. ($if $g = 10 m/s^{2})$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the bob to just complete the vertical circle, the tension at the top just vanishes, so its speed there is $\sqrt{gl}$; energy conservation from the lowest point to the top ($2l$ higher) gives its speed just after the impact:

$v_{b}^{2}=gl+4gl=5gl\Rightarrow v_{b}=\sqrt{5\times 10\times 2}=10\text{m s}^{-1}$

Momentum is conserved during the impact (bullet 0.075 kg, bob 0.050 kg):

$0.075v=0.050\times 10+0.075\times \frac{v}{3}$

$0.075\times \frac{2v}{3}=0.5\Rightarrow 0.05v=0.5\Rightarrow v=10\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 10.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Morning Shift
